A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Video Motion Graphs research work. All 14 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations and supplementary Sections A–G, are readable and support direct comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation and interpolation experiments, an 82-participant user study, and ablations in the main text and supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results, including Tables 1–7 and the supplementary analyses of motion blending, CLIP and ReferenceNet.

M1.justification: Graph construction, searching, HMInterp, training objectives and progressive training remain unchanged. Section 3.1 replaces the named SMPL-X pose source with 'any 3D pose detector', but specifies no replacement component or changed procedure; the graph still operates on the same 3D pose inputs.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same MotionX, Show-Oliver/TED-Talk and Champ data, along with the same dance, gesture, action, interpolation and editing scenarios. No additional pose-detector scenario is actually evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: AnimateAnyone, MagicPose, UniAnimate and MimicMotion in Table 1; the task-specific baselines in Table 2; FILM, VFIFormer, DCInterp and ACInterp in Table 4; and the decoder comparisons in Figure 8. Changed citation numbers identify the same works.

E3.justification: The 367-video test set, masking settings f = 32/64/216, interpolation settings s = 1/3, training schedules, metrics and 82-participant user study are retained. The generic pose-source wording does not report a changed experimental detector or evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The reference-length analysis, motion-guidance and decoder ablations, and progressive-training comparisons are unchanged. Supplementary Section B retains the linear-blending analysis, while Section G retains the CLIP and ReferenceNet ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same reporting practices: point estimates and averaged user preferences, without reported repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–7 and the qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains PSNR 39.53 and FVD 1.210 for HMInterp (s = 1), and supplementary Section B retains the 78% versus 17% linear-blending findings.

T1.justification: The graph-distance definitions, edge threshold, search formulation and supplementary metric equations remain unchanged. The pose-source sentence does not revise the mathematical construction, and no proofs or theoretical results are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about multimodal Video Motion Graphs, HMInterp, progressive training, video quality and supported applications.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 now explicitly presents the pose source as detector-independent, whereas v1 names SMPL-X. This modestly broadens the stated applicability of graph initialization. Interpretations of results and limitations concerning retrieval coverage and dynamic backgrounds remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 identifies SMPL-X and its reference as the source of 3D poses; v2 replaces this with 'any 3D pose detector' without naming the implementation used. This removes specificity from the implementation description. Appendix training details, hardware, runtime figures and project/code information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the SMPL-X citation and the corresponding Pavlakos et al. reference, 'Expressive body capture: 3D hands, face, and body from a single image' (v1 reference 42). Other cited works and research positioning are retained; subsequent references are renumbered.

P1.justification: The pose-source sentence in Section 3.1 is rewritten, and citation numbers and the arXiv version/date are updated. The remaining narrative, section order and supplementary organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–7 retain their displays, placement and captions apart from citation renumbering. Removing the reference causes limited bibliography reflow across PDF pages 10–11, alongside local text wrapping changes.

improvement.justification: The detector-independent wording conveys flexibility, but replacing v1's named SMPL-X pose source and citation with 'any 3D pose detector' leaves graph initialization less traceable. The unchanged appendices provide no replacement implementation detail. This is a limited reproducibility loss; the method, empirical evidence and conclusions otherwise remain unchanged.
